The three exact-distance equations give intersection sizes n-2, four, three, and one. Exact multinomial counts divided by six center orders prove the full polynomial. Its maximum yields the sharp two-list read threshold, while leading positive-profile populations give the sparse asymptotic. A separate direct Hamming-distance brute force checked every unordered triple in dimensions three through eight, including profile collisions. Finite checks supplement rather than replace the infinite combinatorial proof.

Accessible recent primary papers derive general/intersection-specific formulas for Hamming balls or asymptotic three-ball extrema. value.rationale: For exact two-bit substitution reconstruction, knowing the count for one triple does not answer the natural global ambiguity question: which overlap sizes exist and how many triples realize each size? The full all-length polynomial proves a sharp unrestricted two-list read threshold and an asymptotic frequency law for ambiguous triples. It is a complete classification of a natural channel invariant, not an arbitrary finite cutoff or textbook one-line deduction. There is no unsupported coding-rate or biological performance claim.
